ploidyspec report: fCorLav1

Summary

Structure in this individual's assembly, read from the sections below; not inheritance and not origin. See docs/guide, Chapter 6.

Ploidy

2 haplotype copies of each of 40 chromosome numbers; the numbers form sets of 2 (16 homeolog pairs covering 80% of numbers), so x ≈ 20 and up to 4x relative to x.

Confidence: high. Evidence: copies from the assembly (2 per number); 16 homeolog pairs covering 80% of numbers; homeolog distance 0.079 vs unrelated 0.106

Auto-like or allo-like?

One copy apart on most chromosomes, changing haplotype between chromosomes: AAAB-like (one divergent genome copy).

Confidence: medium. Evidence: 32 chromosome numbers assessed: 6 split into lineages, 0 tetrasomic-like, 20 one divergent copy, 6 candidate

TE markers

Only the absolute marker fraction is available (two copies per number); it does not separate diploid, auto- and allopolyploid, so no reading is made from it.

Confidence: not assessable. Evidence: te_marker_fraction mean 0.2096

Rediploidization

Partly: 4 of 32 homeolog-paired chromosome numbers keep stretches of residual tetrasomy (223.1 Mb, 88% of it at chromosome ends) where the homeologs are still as close as alleles; elsewhere they have diverged.

Confidence: medium. Evidence: residual tetrasomy on 4/32 homeolog-paired chromosome numbers, 223.1 Mb, 88% of it terminal; pair-depth CV 0.12

Copy number and copy divergence (whole-chromosome matrix)

Hierarchically reordered, chromosome-number resolution

Same distance data as the heatmaps above, but collapsed to one value per chromosome NUMBER (haplotype copies aggregated away) and reordered by average-linkage clustering -- shows cross-chromosome (subgenome/ancestral-pair) structure cleanly, including diffuse structure with no individually FDR-significant pair. Red outlines mark individually FDR-accepted pairs from the homeolog test below. See INTERPRETATION.md's "checkerboard" section.
